title: Conductor: compact polyglot SDK example hub — Next.js edge, FastAPI, Go server, CLI
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a focused, lightweight examples hub ("Conductor") demonstrating practical SDK patterns across Python, TypeScript, and Go: Next.js edge/ISR example for low-latency streaming, FastAPI server-side batching + dependency injection, idiomatic Go HTTP server with context cancellation and graceful shutdown, and a cross-platform CLI showing ephemeral auth, retry knobs, and streaming consumption. The intent is to provide runnable minimal apps users can copy into their repos and to surface recommended defaults (retry/backoff, streaming ergonomics, token budgeting) without overwhelming users with full-scale reference apps.
acceptance_criteria: Four runnable examples in repo under examples/conductor: next-edge, fastapi-batcher, go-http, cli-tool
Each example includes a README with quick start (docker or local), minimal env vars, and a small test harness
SDK usage demonstrates: streaming handler pattern, connection cancellation, jittered exponential backoff with cap, and a recommended default retry count
Docs PR merged to docs.site with quick copy-paste snippets and a short explainer on streaming memory patterns
Automated smoke tests pass in CI (start example, call API, assert streaming tokens received)
tasks: Create example skeletons and README templates
Implement Python SDK streaming consumer pattern and test harness
Implement TS Next.js edge example with streaming to browser and incremental rendering
Implement Go HTTP server showing context propagation and graceful shutdown
Create CLI example (Go or Python) showing ephemeral key auth + retries
Add CI smoke tests and small e2e workflow
Write docs site snippets and cross-link to SDK reference
comments: 2026-02-10 Maya Chen: Kickoff — aligned with PM: audience is engineers who want copy-paste low-friction examples. Keep each example <250 LOC where possible.

2026-02-12 Arjun Patel: Prototype Python streaming consumer. Decided to expose a streaming iterator (async generator) but also provide a callback helper to avoid keeping full messages in memory for long-running streams. See prototype code in repo: github.com/redwood-inference/examples/conductor/python/stream_consumer.py#L1

2026-02-13 Sofia Martinez (SDK): Reviewed TS Next.js design. Trade-off: Using Edge runtime's ReadableStream API vs React server components. Chose ReadableStream + incremental hydration for broadest compatibility. Note: Deno/Edge had memory leak concerns with generator-based approach; callback pattern preferred for edge workers.

2026-02-14 Arjun Patel: FastAPI example design — using background task to batch similar requests by key for 50ms window. Dependency injector will expose a BatchedClient callable. Added circuit-breaker flag to avoid unbounded queue growth. Confluence design: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Conductor+SDK+Examples

2026-02-15 Maya Chen: Retry policy decision: default to jittered-exponential backoff with base=200ms, factor=2, jitter=0.2, max_attempts=3, max_backoff=4s. Will expose policy object in SDK and show snippet in examples. Rationale: balances latency for interactive flows and protects from hot-looping on 429s. Put in PR for SDK defaults: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2145

2026-02-16 Arjun Patel: CI smoke tests added (workflow: spin up example containers, run small client script to assert streaming tokens). Pushed branch examples/conductor/ci. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/97
